label: Symplectic Manifolds
notes: This chapter spans printed pages 564 to 595 and introduces the symplectic form, a closed nondegenerate two-form. Stress at the outset that this is the geometry of phase space rather than length. The whole arc moves from rigid local algebra toward rich global dynamics, ending near contact geometry.

label: What Is a Symplectic Form
notes: Spell out the two defining conditions carefully. Nondegeneracy is an invertibility statement about the pairing, not positivity, so unlike a metric the form measures oriented area. Closedness is what later powers Darboux and the conservation laws. Emphasize that both axioms are essential and independent.

label: Forced Even Dimension
notes: Walk through why nondegeneracy forces even dimension: a skew matrix in odd dimension is always singular, so it cannot give an invertible pairing. The canonical basis pairs each position vector with its conjugate momentum vector. This is the algebraic heart students must internalize before everything else.

label: The Standard Symplectic Plane
notes: Use the plane as the prototype everyone returns to. Here the symplectic form is exactly the area form dp wedge dq. Point out that symplectomorphisms of the plane are precisely the area and orientation preserving maps. This concrete picture anchors the abstract definition for the rest of the lecture.

label: The Cotangent Bundle as Phase Space
notes: Introduce the tautological one-form, the single most clever construction in the chapter. It is defined coordinate-free yet becomes p dx in any chart. Then the canonical symplectic form is minus its exterior derivative. Emphasize that every cotangent bundle is automatically symplectic, modeling phase space.

label: Darboux's Theorem
notes: State Darboux as the punchline of local theory: every symplectic form looks standard near each point. Contrast sharply with Riemannian geometry, where curvature is a genuine local invariant. The Moser deformation argument connects the given form to the standard one through a clever time dependent vector field.

label: Hamiltonian Vector Fields
notes: Define the Hamiltonian vector field through the interior product equation. Nondegeneracy is exactly what makes this well defined, since it lets us invert the form. In the plane the field rotates around level curves of H. This is where geometry begins to drive dynamics in earnest.

label: Flows Preserve Omega and Energy
notes: Prove the two conservation facts using Cartan's magic formula. The Lie derivative of omega along the Hamiltonian field vanishes because omega is closed, so the flow is symplectic. Energy is conserved because H is constant along its own field. These are the geometric forms of Liouville and energy conservation.

label: The Poisson Bracket
notes: Introduce the Poisson bracket as the antisymmetric pairing of functions through their Hamiltonian fields. It makes smooth functions a Lie algebra and satisfies the Jacobi identity, which follows from closedness. Two functions commute exactly when each is conserved along the other's flow, giving symmetries and conserved quantities.

label: Hamilton's Equations
notes: Connect everything to classical mechanics. In canonical coordinates the Hamiltonian flow is precisely Hamilton's equations, the time evolution of position and momentum. The oscillator gives concentric circular trajectories with conserved energy. Stress that this dictionary is why symplectic geometry is the natural language of mechanics.

label: Symplectic and Lagrangian Submanifolds
notes: Classify submanifolds by how omega restricts to them. Symplectic submanifolds inherit a symplectic structure; isotropic ones kill the form. Lagrangian submanifolds are the maximal isotropic case at half dimension and are central everywhere. Graphs of closed one-forms in the cotangent bundle are the prototypical Lagrangians.

label: A Glimpse of Contact Geometry
notes: Close the theory with the odd dimensional cousin. A contact form is a maximally nondegenerate one-form whose kernel hyperplane field twists as much as possible. On a one jet bundle the canonical contact form detects Legendrian sections, packaging first order partial differential equations geometrically. This points forward to further study.

label: Recap and Takeaways
notes: Summarize the journey: a symplectic form is an invertible alternating area pairing forcing even dimension; cotangent bundles supply the canonical example; Darboux removes all local invariants; Hamiltonian fields and Poisson brackets generate energy preserving dynamics; Lagrangian submanifolds and contact geometry extend the picture. Send students back to the notebook checks.
